# ADR-INV-014 — Platform columns TENANT_ID and VERSION on every INV table
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P2 (Database)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : REQ-INV-001, REQ-INV-003, REQ-INV-035, REQ-INV-037, REQ-INV-043, REQ-INV-078, RULE-INV-002, RULE-INV-006, RULE-INV-030, RULE-INV-036, RULE-INV-045, ENT-INV-001, ENT-INV-002, ENT-INV-003, ENT-INV-004, ENT-INV-005, ENT-INV-006, ENT-INV-007, ENT-INV-008, ENT-INV-009, ENT-INV-010, ENT-INV-011, ENT-INV-012, ENT-INV-013, ENT-INV-014

Filed from db-script-inv.md §5.2, where the decision is recorded in full; the text is unchanged.

## Context
SRS A3 lists no tenant or version field. The given `erp-core` 1.6.0 states the tenancy rule "every table
carries TENANT_ID" and requires every business entity to extend its `AuditableEntity` (TENANT_ID as
Hibernate `@TenantId`, VERSION as the optimistic lock): every table has `TENANT_ID BIGINT NOT NULL`,
`FK_<TABLE>_TENANT → CORE_TENANT(ID)`, an index led by TENANT_ID, every UNIQUE composite with TENANT_ID, and
`VERSION BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. The SRS per-tenant rules (RULE-INV-002, 006, 011, 015, 030, 036, 045)
need a tenant column to hold. NO-COLUMN-INVENTION admits a column the platform mandates for the entity. The
project applied the same rule to PTY (ADR-PTY-035).

## Decision
Every INV table carries TENANT_ID and VERSION as platform columns (DBF-INV-008/009, 020/021, 034/035,
059/060, 081/082, 095/096, 108/109, 123/124, 137/138, 152/153, 169/170, 185/186, 198/199, 214/215), traced
to the entity and to the REQs that create and update its rows. Every UNIQUE leads with TENANT_ID; every
intra-module FK is composite `(TENANT_ID, <FK>)` against a `UQ_<TABLE>_TENANT_PK`; the script is one Flyway
migration with no BEGIN / COMMIT.

## Consequences
- No INV code reads or writes a tenant identifier (the given fills it).
- VERSION gives the optimistic lock that, with the per-Variant serialisation of SRS D-09, keeps concurrent
  moves consistent (REQ-INV-037).
- A later SRS revision may list `tenantId` / `version` in A3's standard fields; no column changes then.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-015.md>>>
# ADR-INV-015 — Currency code on every monetary INV row (profile check CM-8)
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P2 (Database)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : ENT-INV-004, ENT-INV-007, ENT-INV-011, ENT-INV-013, REQ-INV-057, REQ-INV-059, REQ-INV-061, REQ-INV-062, REQ-INV-063, REQ-INV-070, REQ-INV-080, REQ-INV-099, SRS A2 (Currency), SRS D-06

Filed from db-script-inv.md §5.2, where the decision is recorded in full; the text is unchanged.

## Context
Profile check CM-8 (MAJOR) requires every monetary row to carry its currency, "the dimension exists from day
one even while the tenant has one". INV holds amounts on Stock move (unitCost, moveValue), Transfer line
(unitCost), Stock adjustment line (unitCost, lineValue) and Stock valuation (averageUnitCost, stockValue).
SRS A2 and D-06 fix every value "in the tenant base currency" and declare multi-currency an advanced tier,
but A3 holds no currency field.

## Decision
`CURRENCY_CODE VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL` with `CHECK (CURRENCY_CODE ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$')` (ISO 4217) on INV_STOCK_MOVE
(DBF-INV-061), INV_TRANSFER_LINE (DBF-INV-110), INV_STOCK_ADJUSTMENT_LINE (DBF-INV-171) and
INV_STOCK_VALUATION (DBF-INV-200). The service writes the tenant base currency read through the given `cu`
SettingsApi (SRS A9 row 1); there is no column default because the base currency is a tenant setting, not a
constant. INV holds no price, so the price-list part of CM-8 does not apply.

## Consequences
- No SRS meaning changes: every amount stays in the base currency, now stated on the row.
- The stock-move event (CON-INV-020) may add the code as an ADDITIVE field in P3.1.
- When multi-currency arrives, valuation per currency is an additive change.
- A later SRS revision lists `currencyCode` among the fields of the four entities.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-016.md>>>
# ADR-INV-016 — Physical types the SRS leaves open
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P2 (Database)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : DBF-INV-027, DBF-INV-042, DBF-INV-044, DBF-INV-045, DBF-INV-159, DBF-INV-177, DBF-INV-192, DBF-INV-193, DBF-INV-194, REQ-INV-051, REQ-INV-059, REQ-INV-071, REQ-INV-113

Filed from db-script-inv.md §5.2, where the decision is recorded in full; the decision is unchanged (its trace list is written out as ids).

## Context
SRS A3 gives the scale of every decimal (quantity and measure 3, unit and average cost 4, value 2 — D-06) but
no precision; it uses the logical types `date` and `number` (ENT-INV-011.rowNo), which the profile syntax map
lacks, and `lookup` without a length.

## Decision
- Precision 18 for every decimal: `NUMERIC(18,3)` quantities and measures, `NUMERIC(18,4)` costs,
  `NUMERIC(18,2)` values (15 / 14 / 16 integer digits — far above any trader's stock).
- Logical `date` → `DATE` (a calendar date; RULE-INV-038 compares the expiry date with today in the tenant
  time zone, which a timestamp would blur).
- Logical `number` → `INTEGER` (row numbers 1 … 1000, RULE-INV-027).
- Lookup codes → `VARCHAR(50)` (the given `mdl` convention for a stored code).
Each is declared once in the script header. The traces name representative columns; every other NUMERIC,
DATE and lookup column follows the same rule.

## Consequences
- Half-up rounding to the stated scale (SRS D-06) is the service's job; the database stores the scale exactly.
- A base currency with 3 minor units stores values to 2 decimals as SRS D-06 states; changing that is an SRS
  decision ("Change the places per tenant currency").

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-017.md>>>
# ADR-INV-017 — A measure-only adjustment move carries quantity 0
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P2 (Database)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : ENT-INV-004, DBF-INV-042, DBF-INV-043, REQ-INV-123, REQ-INV-099, RULE-INV-017, RULE-INV-034, AC-INV-137

Filed from db-script-inv.md §5.2, where the decision is recorded in full; the text is unchanged.

## Context
SRS ENT-INV-004.quantity is typed "> 0" (RULE-INV-017 for receipts, issues, reservations and transfers),
while REQ-INV-123 posts an adjustment line of a dual-quantity Item whose count change is zero and whose
measure change is non-zero "as a measure-only move" (AC-INV-137: on-hand stays 3, measure 120.500 →
120.000). The move needs a quantity value.

## Decision
`CHK_INV_STOCK_MOVE_QUANTITY`: QUANTITY > 0, or QUANTITY = 0 only on an ADJUSTMENT_IN / ADJUSTMENT_OUT move
whose MEASURE_QTY is greater than 0; the direction of the measure follows the move type, as for the
quantity. Every other move keeps QUANTITY > 0, so RULE-INV-017 holds where it applies.

## Consequences
- A measure-only move has MOVE_VALUE 0 and leaves the average cost unchanged.
- ACC receives it through the stock-move event with quantity 0. P3.1 documents this on CON-INV-020 (no field
  changes).

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-018.md>>>
# ADR-INV-018 — INV v1 uses no given events subscriber and no given file private store
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P2 (repair round 1)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : SRS D-13, SRS D-23, REQ-INV-043, REQ-INV-051, REQ-INV-052, REQ-INV-070, REQ-INV-071, REQ-INV-073

## Context
`gov.py analyze` (P2 round 1, C-GIVEN-2 given-via-extension) reported two MAJOR findings on the SRS:
it names `com.erp.events.OutboxSubscriber` (erp-core:modules.events) and
`com.erp.file.crossmodule.FilePrivateStoreApi` (erp-core:modules.file) and no `given-usage` row declares either use.

Both names appear only in the "Override / status" column of SRS "Decisions applied", i.e. as the
alternative that was **not** chosen:
- D-23 — chosen: PUR, SLS and SFR call INV operations; INV subscribes to none of their events (DAG stays
  downward-only). Override: "Subscribe to their events through OutboxSubscriber".
- D-13 — chosen: the browser reads the xlsx opening stock sheet and submits 1–1000 rows; INV parses no
  uploaded file. Override: "Server-side import through FilePrivateStoreApi when the core publishes the read".

No REQ, RULE, contract item, table, column, seed row or XM of INV v1 uses either interface.

## Decision
Take the finding's "stop using it" branch, not "add the row". INV v1 declares no use of either interface;
the `given-usage` blocks of the SRS and the contract are left unchanged, because a row would declare a use
that does not exist (and, for the subscriber, invite an upward dependency the DAG forbids).

The two SRS override cells are to be reworded at the next touch of P1 so that they describe the
alternative without naming the interface, with no meaning change:
- D-23 override → "Subscribe to their events through the given events module"
- D-13 override → "Server-side import through the given file module once the core publishes the read"

Adopting either alternative later is an SRS change that adds the matching `given-usage` row to the SRS
and repeats it in the contract in the same change.

## Consequences
- P2 is structurally unchanged: DBF-INV-001 … DBF-INV-219 and XM-INV-001 … XM-INV-013 stay as written.
- The P2 artifacts (db-script-inv.md §5.2 / §5.3, registry-db-inv.md Decisions) record this decision.
- The finding is raised on SRS text, which P2 does not write; it clears when the two P1 cells above are
  reworded.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-019.md>>>
# ADR-INV-019 — P2 cannot clear the C-GIVEN-2 findings raised on the P1 SRS text; the pass stops
Status      : ACCEPTED (unblocked 2026-10-31)
Stage       : P2 (repair round 2)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : ADR-INV-018, SRS D-13, SRS D-23, REQ-INV-043, REQ-INV-051, REQ-INV-052, REQ-INV-070, REQ-INV-071, REQ-INV-073

## Context
`gov.py analyze` refused P2 twice (round 1 and repair round 1) with the same two MAJOR C-GIVEN-2
(given-via-extension) findings on artifact `srs`:
- `srs` names `OutboxSubscriber` (erp-core:modules.events) with no `given-usage` row;
- `srs` names `FilePrivateStoreApi` (erp-core:modules.file) with no `given-usage` row.

Repair round 1 took the finding's "stop using it" branch (ADR-INV-018, ACCEPTED). INV v1 uses neither
interface: the names sit only in the "Override / status" column of SRS "Decisions applied", rows D-23 and
D-13. That column lists the alternative that was **not** chosen. ADR-INV-018 gave the replacement wording for
the two cells, but the cells are in the SRS (`analysis/modules/INV/P1/srs-inv.md`, carried into
`_state/current-srs.md`). P2 does not own the SRS and its write set is the two P2 files. Neither P2 file
names either interface. The check reads the SRS text only, so no edit to a P2 artifact can change its result.
A further P2 repair round would produce the same refusal.

Both of the finding's remedies need a P1 change:
- "add the row" — the SRS `given-usage` block and the contract `given-usage` block (P1, P1.5);
- "stop using it" — reword the two SRS override cells (P1).

## Decision
Stop the P2 pass as BLOCKED rather than run another repair round that cannot succeed.
- ADR-INV-018 stands: INV v1 declares no use of either interface. Adding `given-usage` rows would declare
  uses that do not exist, and for the subscriber it would invite an upward dependency that the DAG forbids.
- The P2 artifacts are complete and are kept as written. DBF-INV-001 … DBF-INV-219, XM-INV-001 …
  XM-INV-013, the SQL script, the seed blocks and ADR-INV-014 … 018 are unchanged. Only the decision
  records cite this ADR.
- This is not a structural or meaning conflict with the SRS. It is BLOCKED because the stage's exit
  condition depends on an artifact the stage does not own.

## Unblock condition
Reword the two cells in the P1 SRS through a P1 repair or an authorised edit of
`analysis/modules/INV/P1/srs-inv.md`, then regenerate `_state/current-srs.md`. The meaning of the cells
stays the same:
- D-23 "Override / status": `Subscribe to their events through OutboxSubscriber` →
  `Subscribe to their events through the given events module`
- D-13 "Override / status": `Server-side import through FilePrivateStoreApi when the core publishes the read` →
  `Server-side import through the given file module once the core publishes the read`

Then re-run `gov.py analyze` for P2. No P2 file needs to change for the findings to clear. When they clear,
this ADR becomes ACCEPTED (unblocked) and P2 proceeds to P3.1.

## Consequences
- P2 does not pass its gate until the unblock condition holds. P3.1 does not start.
- No DBF, XM, table, column, constraint or seed row changes, now or when the unblock condition holds.
- The contract (P1.5) needs no change under the "stop using it" branch, because neither name appears in it.

## Status
BLOCKED — stop the pass. The stage's exit condition depends on a P1 artifact outside the P2 write set.

## Resolution (2026-10-31, under Hesham's standing authorisation)
The unblock condition holds. Factory fix `149c8d5` lets a stage repair edit the earlier file a finding
names. The re-run P2 repair reworded the two SRS cells exactly as stated above, with no change of meaning
(ADR-INV-020). `gov.py analyze stage:P2` now reports 0 critical · 0 major · 0 minor. No P2 artifact
changed for the unblock. Status: ACCEPTED, so P2 proceeds to P3.1.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-020.md>>>
# ADR-INV-020 — The SRS D-13 and D-23 override cells name no given interface (C-GIVEN-2 cleared on the SRS side)
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P2 (repair round 1 of the re-run)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : ADR-INV-018, ADR-INV-019, SRS D-13, SRS D-23, REQ-INV-043, REQ-INV-051, REQ-INV-052, REQ-INV-070, REQ-INV-071, REQ-INV-073

## Context
`gov.py analyze` refused P2 again with the same two MAJOR C-GIVEN-2 (given-via-extension) findings on
artifact `srs`. The SRS names `OutboxSubscriber` (erp-core:modules.events) and `FilePrivateStoreApi`
(erp-core:modules.file), and no `given-usage` row declares either use. ADR-INV-018 chose the finding's
"stop using it" branch. ADR-INV-019 stopped the pass because the fix belongs in the P1 SRS, which P2 did not
own. This repair brief authorises an in-place edit of `analysis/modules/INV/P1/srs-inv.md` for these
findings, which is the unblock condition ADR-INV-019 names.

The finding offers two fixes. One is to add the `given-usage` rows to the SRS and repeat them in the
contract. The other is to stop using the interfaces.

## Decision
Stop using the interfaces, as ADR-INV-018 decided. INV v1 uses neither interface: both names appear only
in the "Override / status" column of SRS "Decisions applied", which lists the alternative that was not
chosen. A `given-usage` row would declare a use that does not exist. For the subscriber, it would also
invite an upward dependency on PUR, SLS and SFR that the DAG forbids.

The two cells are reworded with no change of meaning, using the wording that ADR-INV-018 and ADR-INV-019 gave:
- D-13 "Override / status": `Server-side import through FilePrivateStoreApi when the core publishes the read` →
  `Server-side import through the given file module once the core publishes the read`
- D-23 "Override / status": `Subscribe to their events through OutboxSubscriber` →
  `Subscribe to their events through the given events module`

The `given-usage` blocks of the SRS (A9) and the contract (§2.5) are unchanged and stay identical. The
contract names neither interface.

## Consequences
- The two C-GIVEN-2 findings are fixed on the SRS side. No P1 file names either interface.
- The unblock condition of ADR-INV-019 now holds once `_state/current-srs.md` is regenerated from the
  edited SRS. ADR-INV-019 is not rewritten under its id; its resolution (BLOCKED → ACCEPTED) is left to the
  human who owns it.
- No DBF, XM, table, column, constraint, seed row, REQ, RULE, ENT or contract item changes.
- If either alternative is adopted later, that is an SRS change. It adds the matching `given-usage` row to
  the SRS and repeats it in the contract in the same change.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-021.md>>>
# ADR-INV-021 — Infrastructure errors are PLATFORM-STD catalog rows
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : REQ-INV-138, AC-INV-154, API-INV-001 … API-INV-051

## Context
The engine requires infrastructure errors (not found, forbidden, server) to be Error Catalog rows with
RULE = PLATFORM-STD and an ADR. The SRS gives a text only for the forbidden case (AC-INV-154). Optimistic
locking on VERSION (ADR-INV-014) and malformed requests also produce errors that no RULE covers.

## Decision
The catalog carries these PLATFORM-STD rows, every code an instance of `{MOD}-{http}[-{SLUG}]`:
INV-400 (malformed request), INV-401 (unauthenticated — the given security filter), INV-403 (forbidden —
message of AC-INV-154 verbatim), INV-404-{WAREHOUSE|BRANCH|VARIANT|ITEM|STOCK-MOVE|TRANSFER|STOCK-COUNT|
STOCK-COUNT-LINE|STOCK-ADJUSTMENT|LOT}-NOT-FOUND, INV-409-STALE-VERSION (OptimisticLockException) and INV-500.
Rows other than INV-403 carry no text: their messages are the platform's own `LocalizedException` texts,
not invented here. Translation of exceptions is central (CORE): constraint-name mapping for UNIQUE
violations, optimistic lock → INV-409-STALE-VERSION, anything else → INV-500.

## Consequences
- Every operation of api-spec-inv.yaml answers 400, 401, 403 and 500 with these codes.
- The message bundle needs the platform texts for the rows without SRS text; the implementer takes them from
  the given erp-core message catalog.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-022.md>>>
# ADR-INV-022 — The consumed unit-of-measure lookup key is configured, not hardcoded
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : ENT-INV-014, DBF-INV-208, RULE-INV-041, REQ-INV-125, API-INV-045

## Context
ENT-INV-014.measureUomCode stores a code of the unit-of-measure lookup owned by the Item owner module
(SRS A6 "Lookups consumed"). The SRS names the key only as "CAT unit-of-measure key"; it does not spell the
key string. The binding rule forbids inventing it, and lookup values must be loaded at runtime from mdl.

## Decision
The service validates measureUomCode as an active value of the key named by the configuration property
`inv.lookup.measure-uom-key`, through `MdlLookupApi`. The deployment sets the property from the key owner's
published registry. The key string is PENDING in this plan; no value is hardcoded in INV. While the
property is unset, a non-empty measureUomCode is refused with INV-422-MEASURE-UNIT-REQUIRED.

## Consequences
- RULE-INV-041 (and the CHECK CHK_INV_ITEM_STOCK_SETTINGS_MEASURE_UOM_CODE) is enforced from day one; the
  value check becomes complete once the property is set.
- If the key owner later publishes the key in its contract, this ADR is superseded by a plan update that
  names it.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-023.md>>>
# ADR-INV-023 — Cross-module foreign keys reference the target's primary key column only
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : XM-INV-001 … XM-INV-011, CON-CAT-001, CON-CAT-002, db-script D-P2-14

## Context
The db-script declares the eleven HARD-FK columns column-only and leaves the constraint to the INT-C blocks;
its D-P2-14 expected the constraints to be composite with TENANT_ID. The CAT contract promises a BIGINT
identifier for Item and Variant but, by design, no table, column list or tenant-scoped unique key. A composite
FK needs a UNIQUE (TENANT_ID, <pk>) on the target that nothing promises.

## Decision
Each ddl_patch is a single-column foreign key from this module's column to the target primary key:
`REFERENCES CAT_VARIANT (VARIANT_PK)` for the ten Variant columns and `REFERENCES CAT_ITEM (ITEM_PK)` for
INV_ITEM_STOCK_SETTINGS.ITEM_FK. The table and key names are derived from the shared naming rule
(`<MOD>_` + entity in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, PK `<entity>_PK`). Before running a patch the executor checks both
names against the delivered target migration and runs the orphan pre-check in the block's config line.
Tenant correctness of the reference is ensured by reading the Variant / Item through the tenant-scoped
in-process reads (XM-INV-014, XM-INV-015) before every write.

## Consequences
- Every patch can be applied to any delivered target without a target change.
- If the target later publishes a tenant-scoped unique key, a later version may replace the patches with
  composite FKs (a new ddl_patch per edge).

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-024.md>>>
# ADR-INV-024 — The contract operations are one in-process bean with no REST surface
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : CON-INV-006 … CON-INV-021, RULE-INV-020, RULE-INV-021, RULE-INV-023, RULE-INV-039, REQ-INV-043 … REQ-INV-058

## Context
The contract promises sixteen operations and two events to other modules, all in-process
(conventions.module_interface: in_process). Several of them (reserve, release, receive, issue) have no
screen and no REST endpoint in SRS B5. Four rules are raised only on those paths (RULE-INV-020, 021, 023,
039). The Error Catalog block is derived into HTTP responses, and the QR catalog requires every entry to be
reached by an API-* block.

## Decision
- One Spring bean `com.erp.inv.crossmodule.InventoryApi` honours CON-INV-006 … 019; the events CON-INV-020,
  021 go through OutboxPublisher. No method has a REST route.
- The four codes raised only in-process (INV-409-RESERVE-NOT-AVAILABLE, INV-409-RESERVATION-CLOSED,
  INV-409-STOCK-MOVE-IMMUTABLE, INV-422-LOT-EXPIRED) are listed in plan §5.1 and in the API document's
  document-level `x-inprocess-error-codes`, not in the HTTP catalog block, because no operation can answer
  them.
- Repository operations reached only in-process (reservation insert / lock / update / by key / by document,
  moves by idempotency key) are stated as intents R-1 … R-6 in SVC-API-INT, not as QR entries.

## Consequences
- api-spec-errors holds only codes an HTTP operation can raise.
- The calling modules receive these codes as LocalizedException and surface them on their own endpoints.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-025.md>>>
# ADR-INV-025 — Native aggregate searches; Variant term and Item filters through in-process reads
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : QR-INV-015, QR-INV-016, QR-INV-038, REQ-INV-038, REQ-INV-039, REQ-INV-109, REQ-INV-116, API-INV-016, API-INV-017, API-INV-040, API-INV-050

## Context
Reserved and available quantities are derived (SRS A3): available = on-hand outside expired lots minus
ACTIVE reservations. The lot screen needs on-hand per lot and warehouse. Both need joins of INV_STOCK_BALANCE
with INV_LOT and INV_RESERVATION, and a join needs an ADR. The balance and valuation screens filter by
"Variant (code, name or barcode)" and by Item; the Variant and Item records belong to another module, which
publishes a barcode lookup, Item reads and an Item search, but no Variant search by code or name.

## Decision
- QR-INV-015, 016 and 038 are native aggregate queries with LEFT JOINs to INV_LOT and an aggregated
  sub-select of ACTIVE INV_RESERVATION rows; all are read-only and paged where they list.
- The `term` filter is resolved as a barcode through XM-INV-013; `itemPk` and Item terms resolve to Variant /
  Item identifiers through XM-INV-015; Variant display names are read per page through XM-INV-014. Picking a
  Variant by code or name is done in the frontend with the owner module's picker, which yields variantPk.

## Consequences
- No view or routine is added to the database (db-script BLOCK 9 / 10 stay empty).
- Search by Variant code text on the balance screen works through the picker, not through free text.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-026.md>>>
# ADR-INV-026 — Locking order, insert-if-absent and serialisation points
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : REQ-INV-037, REQ-INV-008, REQ-INV-027, REQ-INV-006, REQ-INV-044, REQ-INV-088, SRS D-09, QR-INV-002, QR-INV-005, QR-INV-012, QR-INV-017, QR-INV-023, QR-INV-024, QR-INV-031, QR-INV-040, QR-INV-041

## Context
Parallel channels move the same Variant in the same warehouse (REQ-INV-037); the negative-stock and
reservation checks read a value and then write; two default switches, two first lots of one number, two scans
of one Variant and a deactivation racing a post must all stay consistent. "Validated first" is not a guard.

## Decision
- Balance rows: INSERT … ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT UQ_INV_STOCK_BALANCE_VAR_WH_LOT DO NOTHING, then SELECT …
  FOR UPDATE, all rows of a document in ascending (VARIANT_FK, WAREHOUSE_FK, LOT_FK NULLS FIRST) order;
  valuation rows next, ascending VARIANT_FK, the same way on UQ_INV_STOCK_VALUATION_VARIANT_FK. Checks read
  after the locks.
- Reservations and issues of a Variant × warehouse serialise on the lot-less balance row of the pair.
- Posting paths read the warehouse FOR SHARE; deactivation takes it FOR UPDATE before its usage probe. The
  same pattern guards a branch against a concurrent warehouse save.
- Default switches lock the current default first (partial unique indexes back them).
- Document headers are locked FOR UPDATE before any status check (post / cancel / line change).
- Lots: SELECT … FOR UPDATE by (VARIANT_FK, CODE) and insert-if-absent on UQ_INV_LOT_VAR_CODE.
- Numbers come atomically from NumberSeriesApi; masters use optimistic VERSION for edits.

## Consequences
- No lost update, no double-pass of a check, no deadlock between documents (one global lock order).
- Large opening stock loads hold many row locks for one transaction; acceptable at ≤ 1000 rows.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-027.md>>>
# ADR-INV-027 — Opening stock is created and posted in one call, all rows or none
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : REQ-INV-070, REQ-INV-071, REQ-INV-072, REQ-INV-073, REQ-INV-074, RULE-INV-027, RULE-INV-028, SRS D-13, API-INV-046, API-INV-047

## Context
SRS D-13: opening stock is a Stock adjustment with reason OPENING_STOCK; the browser reads the xlsx sheet
and submits 1–1000 rows; all rows post or none; failing rows are reported with their row number. A row names
"Variant code or barcode". The Variant owner publishes a barcode lookup but no lookup by Variant code.

## Decision
- POST /api/v1/inv/opening-stock creates one OPENING_STOCK adjustment and posts it in the same transaction
  (201 with the posted adjustment).
- A row identifies its Variant by `variantPk` (the browser resolves a code through the owner's picker or reads)
  or by `barcode` (resolved through XM-INV-013).
- Every row is validated before anything is written. Any failure answers 422 INV-422-LOAD-ROWS-INVALID
  (rule REQ-INV-072) with `details[]` = {rowNo, code, messageAr, messageEn} per failing row, each code one of
  the catalog's row codes. A load with 0 or more than 1000 rows answers INV-422-LOAD-ROWS.
- The sheet (API-INV-046) is report INV_OPENING_STOCK_SHEET rendered by PrintApi, with the lot, expiry and
  measure columns only when their flags are on.

## Consequences
- A resubmitted identical load creates a second adjustment; the screen prevents double submission.
- No uploaded file is stored or parsed by INV (ADR-INV-018 stands).

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-028.md>>>
# ADR-INV-028 — Inventory settings and context endpoints
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : REQ-INV-065, REQ-INV-066, REQ-INV-118, REQ-INV-119, REQ-INV-010, REQ-INV-029, REQ-INV-132, REQ-INV-134, REQ-INV-135, SRS D-04, API-INV-008, API-INV-048, API-INV-049

## Context
The negative-stock setting and the near-expiry horizon are given cu settings (SRS D-04), not INV columns;
REQ-INV-119 bounds the horizon to whole days 1–365 with a message, but no RULE carries the range. Every
screen must know the active warehouse and branch counts and the capability flags to hide or show controls.

## Decision
- GET / PUT /api/v1/inv/settings read and write INV_ALLOW_NEGATIVE_STOCK and INV_NEAR_EXPIRY_DAYS through
  SettingsApi (tenant override over the platform defaults seeded in db-script BLOCK 8e).
- An out-of-range horizon answers 422 INV-422-HORIZON-RANGE with the REQ-INV-119 / AC-INV-133 text; the
  catalog row names rule REQ-INV-119.
- GET /api/v1/inv/context answers activeWarehouseCount, activeBranchCount, lotExpiryFl, dualQuantityFl,
  bundlesFl; it requires any INV page VIEW permission.

## Consequences
- The settings screen has no INV entity; its permission-matrix row names ENT-INV-004, whose moves the
  negative-stock setting governs.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-029.md>>>
# ADR-INV-029 — Item stock settings are saved by an idempotent PUT keyed by Item
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : ENT-INV-014, REQ-INV-124, REQ-INV-125, REQ-INV-129, RULE-INV-045, DBF-INV-210, DBF-INV-211, DBF-INV-212, API-INV-045

## Context
SRS B5 gives one save operation, PUT …/item-stock-settings/by-item/{itemId}, for both creating the record of
an Item and changing it; B4 grants CREATE and UPDATE separately. key, valueAr and valueEn are NOT NULL and
system-filled; the SRS gives only examples of the summary text («تشغيلة وصلاحية» / "Lot and expiry").

## Decision
- The PUT creates the record when none exists (requires PERM_INV_ITEM_STOCK_SETTINGS_CREATE) and updates it
  otherwise (requires PERM_INV_ITEM_STOCK_SETTINGS_UPDATE and the version).
- key = the Item's code (read through XM-INV-015). valueAr / valueEn = a summary built from the flags:
  lot-tracked → «تشغيلة وصلاحية» / "Lot and expiry"; dual-quantity → «كمية مزدوجة» / "Dual quantity"; both →
  the two joined with « · » / " · "; neither → «بدون تتبع» / "No tracking". isActiveFl = true.

## Consequences
- A concurrent first save is caught by UQ_INV_ITEM_STOCK_SETTINGS_ITEM_FK and retried as an update.
- The summary texts are display data, not messages; they can be changed without a rule change.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-030.md>>>
# ADR-INV-030 — "Never valued" means no valuation row; how the row is created
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : RULE-INV-025, REQ-INV-059, REQ-INV-060, REQ-INV-061, REQ-INV-064, REQ-INV-066, ENT-INV-013, QR-INV-019, QR-INV-023, QR-INV-024

## Context
RULE-INV-025 refuses a costless incoming line when "the Variant has no Stock valuation". Negative stock is
allowed by default (REQ-INV-066), so a Variant can be issued before it was ever received; its outgoing moves
need a unit cost (UNIT_COST is NOT NULL) although no average exists. Creating a valuation row with average 0
on that issue would let later costless receipts enter at 0, which RULE-INV-025 forbids.

## Decision
- "Never valued" ≡ no INV_STOCK_VALUATION row for the Variant.
- An outgoing move (or transfer leg) of a never-valued Variant is recorded at unit cost 0 and value 0 and
  creates no valuation row.
- The first incoming valued move creates the row with TOTAL_ON_HAND_QTY = the Variant's on-hand over all
  warehouses after the move (QR-INV-019, which may reflect earlier negative issues), AVERAGE_UNIT_COST = the
  move's unit cost (consistent with REQ-INV-060), STOCK_VALUE = total × average, DOC_DATE = the move date.

## Consequences
- RULE-INV-025 keeps its meaning; the valuation total always equals the on-hand sum once the row exists.
- Issues before the first valued receipt carry cost 0 in the stock-move event; the ledger owner sees them
  as such.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-031.md>>>
# ADR-INV-031 — Two SOFT-READ edges minted at P3.1 (Variant and Item state reads)
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : XM-INV-014, XM-INV-015, RULE-INV-018, RULE-INV-028, RULE-INV-042, RULE-INV-043, RULE-INV-045, REQ-INV-052, REQ-INV-124, REQ-INV-129, CON-CAT-001, CON-CAT-002, CON-CAT-007, CON-CAT-008, CON-CAT-016

## Context
The P2 register holds eleven HARD-FK edges to the Variant and Item of the catalogue module (structural: the
access is the key) and two SOFT-READ edges (bundle components, barcodes). This stage's runtime checks are the
first reads of the Variant's and the Item's state: active Variant of a STANDARD Item (RULE-INV-018, 028),
BUNDLE refusal and Item code for the settings key (RULE-INV-045), the Item's Variants for RULE-INV-042 / 043
and the Item filters, and display names. No registered edge carries that read, and a HARD-FK block's adapter
line is not the place for it.

## Decision
Mint two edges in INT-C, continuing the XM sequence:
- XM-INV-014 SOFT-READ → CAT · ENT-CAT-002 (contract CON-CAT-002), through getVariant (CON-CAT-008) and
  getItem (CON-CAT-007), port `VariantReadPort`.
- XM-INV-015 SOFT-READ → CAT · ENT-CAT-001 (contract CON-CAT-001), through getItem (CON-CAT-007) and
  searchCatalogue (CON-CAT-016), port `ItemReadPort`.
Both point downward (CAT is DAG #1). The orchestrator back-registers them into the register in this run
(records in registry-exec-be-inv.md, `xm-minted`).

## Consequences
- Every runtime read of another module's data is tracked by one edge and one package.
- The XM total of the db-script stays 13; the plan carries 15 blocks.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-032.md>>>
# ADR-INV-032 — State-change PATCH endpoints carry the caller's version as a typed body
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.1 (Backend Execution Plan · repair round 1)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : API-INV-006, API-INV-007, API-INV-014, API-INV-015, API-INV-024, API-INV-032, API-INV-038, DBF-INV-009, DBF-INV-021, DBF-INV-096, DBF-INV-124, DBF-INV-153, REQ-INV-007, REQ-INV-008, REQ-INV-026, REQ-INV-027, REQ-INV-080, REQ-INV-092, REQ-INV-099, ADR-INV-014, ADR-INV-021

## Context
`gov.py analyze` (C7.31 api-spec-valid) refused the API document: seven PATCH operations — reactivate and
set-default of a warehouse and of a branch, and post of a transfer, a stock count and a stock adjustment —
had no typed `requestBody`. The plan wrote them as "path id · no body". The SRS B5 rows list only `id` as
input. Each of these actions changes a versioned record (VERSION, ADR-INV-014). The record may have changed
since the caller read it: a DRAFT edited by another user, a default moved by another Owner.

## Decision
Each of the seven endpoints takes one shared, typed body `VersionedActionRequest {version}` (int64, required,
no other property). `version` is the VERSION of the record the action targets: DBF-INV-009 for a warehouse,
DBF-INV-021 for a branch, DBF-INV-096 for a transfer, DBF-INV-124 for a stock count, DBF-INV-153 for a stock
adjustment. For set-default it is the target's version. The service checks it after locking the row. A
mismatch answers the existing catalog row INV-409-STALE-VERSION (PLATFORM-STD, ADR-INV-021), which now lists
the seven endpoints.

This is the platform's optimistic-lock pattern, already used by every PUT of the module. A body that only
satisfies the schema (an empty object) was rejected: it would carry nothing, and the race it leaves open is
real. Posting a draft whose lines another user has just changed would move stock the poster never saw.

## Consequences
- The plan's Request, Errors and Orchestration lines and `traces=` of API-INV-006, 007, 014, 015, 024, 032
  and 038 name the version DBF. The API document derives the body, the 409 response and `x-traces` from them.
- The frontend sends the version it read with each of these actions, as it already does on save.
- No SRS meaning, RULE, REQ, table or column changes. SRS B5 lists inputs by meaning; the version is the
  platform concurrency token, not a business input.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-033.md>>>
# ADR-INV-033 — Reads a screen needs that are not operations of api-spec-inv.yaml
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : UXD-INV-001, UXD-INV-002, UXD-INV-003, UXD-INV-004, UXD-INV-005, UXD-INV-006, UXD-INV-007, UXD-INV-008, UXD-INV-009, UXD-INV-010, UXD-INV-011, REQ-INV-039, REQ-INV-075, REQ-INV-078, REQ-INV-088, REQ-INV-091, REQ-INV-097, REQ-INV-109, REQ-INV-121, REQ-INV-124, REQ-INV-125, REQ-INV-063, REQ-INV-138, API-INV-008, ADR-INV-024

## Context
The frontend plan binds every read of a screen to an operation of `api-spec-inv.yaml` (C9.24). Three kinds of
read that INV screens need are not in that document, and cannot be:

1. **Catalogue data owned by CAT.** A transfer, adjustment or count line carries `variantPk` only
   (`TransferLine`, `StockAdjustmentLine`, `StockCountLine`); a lot row carries `variantPk` only (`LotRow`);
   the balance row carries no Item. Choosing a Variant or an Item (pickers, barcode entry) and labelling a
   `variantPk` need CAT reads: search (CON-CAT-016), barcode lookup (CON-CAT-010), read Variant (CON-CAT-008),
   read Item (CON-CAT-007). The CAT unit-of-measure lookup labels `measureUomCode` (SRS A6, lookups consumed).
2. **Lookup values** of the INV_* keys (INV_ADJUSTMENT_REASON, INV_MOVE_TYPE, INV_DOC_STATUS,
   INV_SOURCE_DOC_TYPE). SRS A6: they are loaded at runtime from the given core lookup module `mdl`.
3. **The user's permissions.** The platform security module (`sec`, given) derives `PERM_<PAGE_CODE>_<ACTION>`
   and the session carries them. No INV operation returns them.

## Decision
- Each CAT read a screen needs is a **UXD** (UXD-INV-001 … 011), minted in the ui-ux-spec and cited by the F-blocks.
  The UXD names the owner module and the CAT contract (CON-CAT-xxx). It cites no CAT API id and no CAT path.
  The id and path are CAT's and resolve in CAT's own artifacts at build time. In the screen-hooks blocks
  these reads are `kind: lookup` hooks with no `api` binding.
- INV_* lookup values are read through one shared `kind: lookup` hook per key. The hook is served by the given
  `mdl` surface and has no `api` binding.
- Permissions are read from the authenticated session (given `sec`) by each screen's `SCREEN-INIT` hook. That hook
  is bound to API-INV-008 (active counts and capability flags) for the rest of its job.
- The frontend executor's mock server serves `api-spec-inv.yaml`. It also stubs the CAT reads, the `mdl` lookup
  values and the session permissions from fixtures. These fixtures are not part of the INV API document.

## Consequences
- No hook of kind `read` cites an operation outside `api-spec-inv.yaml`.
- A user without a CAT read grant gets no picker results. The picker shows the INV-403 catalogue message. INV does
  not widen CAT's grants.
- No REQ, RULE, field, permission or API changes.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-034.md>>>
# ADR-INV-034 — The stock count entry commits line by line
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : SCR-INV-006, REQ-INV-087, REQ-INV-088, REQ-INV-089, REQ-INV-090, REQ-INV-091, REQ-INV-092, AC-INV-097, AC-INV-099, AC-INV-100, API-INV-028, API-INV-029, API-INV-030, API-INV-031, API-INV-032, ADR-INV-032

## Context
The screen-composition rule says a screen opened to edit ONE record has ONE save. A page also keeps its child
lines inline, and their edits return to the form state until that one save. The stock count is designed
differently in the SRS and the API document. "Start count" creates the DRAFT (API-INV-028). Each scan **adds to
the server line** of that Variant (REQ-INV-088, AC-INV-097: scanning 1 and then 2 gives one line of 3). Changing
or removing a line is its own operation (API-INV-030 / 031). There is no operation that saves a whole count with
its lines, and no header field can change after "Start count". If scans were collected in the browser and saved
once, a phone that loses its page loses the count. Repeated scans could not add up on the server either.

## Decision
- SCR-INV-006 is a `page` with its lines `inline`, as the container rule says. Its submit is **the line
  action**. Each scan sends one API-INV-029 call. The one-line drawer opened from a line (change countedQty or
  countedMeasureQty, or remove) sends one API-INV-030 or 031 on confirm. One user action never sends two calls.
- "Start count", "Post" and "Cancel" are state transitions of the document, not saves. Post and Cancel carry the
  version the screen last read (ADR-INV-032).
- After each line call the screen re-reads the count (API-INV-027). It shows the server's line, not a local copy.

## Consequences
- The count entry has no form-level Save button. The one-save rule holds per action, and no surface holds unsaved
  line edits.
- The one-line drawer of a count line saves on confirm. This differs from the transfer and adjustment drawers,
  which return a value to the form. The F4 block of SCR-INV-006 states this.
- No REQ, RULE, field or API changes.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-035.md>>>
# ADR-INV-035 — The browser reads the opening stock sheet
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : SCR-INV-010, REQ-INV-071, REQ-INV-072, REQ-INV-073, AC-INV-077, AC-INV-078, AC-INV-079, AC-INV-080, API-INV-046, API-INV-047, ADR-INV-027

## Context
DEFAULT D-13 (SRS): "the browser reads the filled sheet and submits its rows". INV parses no uploaded file.
API-INV-046 returns the xlsx sheet. API-INV-047 takes `rows` (1–1000), and each row has `rowNo`, `variantPk` or
`barcode`, `quantity`, `unitCost`, `lotNo`, `lotExpiryDate` and `measureQty`. Two points are left open:

1. `profile.stack.frontend` names no library that reads an xlsx file.
2. The sheet has one column, «رمز المتغيّر أو الباركود» / "Variant code or barcode" (AC-INV-080). The request
   has a `barcode` field and a `variantPk` field, and no Variant-code field.

## Decision
1. The opening stock screen reads the xlsx file with a spreadsheet-reading library added to the frontend stack.
   The library is loaded only in that screen's lazy chunk, and the screen is its only user. The implementer
   chooses a maintained library that reads xlsx client-side. Nothing is uploaded.
2. The text of the "Variant code or barcode" cell is sent **unchanged in `barcode`**, and `variantPk` stays null.
   The backend resolves the text to one active Variant (RULE-INV-028, INV-422-LOAD-ROW-VARIANT, reported with its
   `rowNo`). The browser does not resolve rows through CAT.
3. Columns are matched by their header text in either language (ar or en), as the sheet (AC-INV-080) defines them.
   `rowNo` is the sheet row number that the Owner sees.
4. The browser checks the row count (1–1000, RULE-INV-027) before sending, using the RULE-INV-027 message. It sends
   all rows in one call (ADR-INV-027). Row failures in `details` are listed by `rowNo` with their messages.

## Consequences
- One new frontend dependency, scoped to SCR-INV-010.
- If P3.1 meant `barcode` to carry barcodes only, this is the open point. The backend plan's RULE-INV-028 check
  already covers "code or barcode", so this stage changes no operation.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-036.md>>>
# ADR-INV-036 — Warehouse and lot labels on the stock balance screen for a Seller/Cashier
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P3.2 (Frontend — UX Design + Execution Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : analysis · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : SCR-INV-003, REQ-INV-012, REQ-INV-039, REQ-INV-040, REQ-INV-137, AC-INV-044, AC-INV-153, API-INV-001, API-INV-016, API-INV-017, API-INV-040

## Context
SCR-INV-003 (Stock balances) is the only INV page a Seller/Cashier sees. B4 gives that role
`PERM_INV_STOCK_BALANCES_VIEW` only. The balance row (`StockBalanceRow`) and the availability answer
(`Availability.perWarehouse`) carry `warehousePk` but no warehouse code or name. Labelling that id or offering
the warehouse filter needs API-INV-001, which requires `PERM_INV_WAREHOUSES_VIEW`, and a Seller/Cashier does not
hold it. The lot filter has the same problem: its options come from API-INV-040, which requires
`PERM_INV_LOTS_VIEW`. The lot column itself is fine, because the row carries `lotCode`.

AC-INV-044 expects a Seller/Cashier to read rows "W1 … W2" by warehouse. Showing a bare identifier would fail it.

## Decision
- Frontend, now: the warehouse column and the warehouse filter are labelled through the shared warehouse lookup
  (API-INV-001, `active=ALL`) when the user holds `PERM_INV_WAREHOUSES_VIEW` (Owner, Warehouse). For a user
  without it, the warehouse label is **PENDING ADR-INV-036**. The column shows the identifier, and the filter is
  not offered. The lot filter is offered only with `PERM_INV_LOTS_VIEW`. The lot column is always shown, from
  `lotCode`.
- Backend gap, named here: `StockBalanceRow` and `Availability.perWarehouse` should carry `warehouseCode`,
  `warehouseNameAr` and `warehouseNameEn`. The P3.1 delta adds them, and the frontend then reads the label from
  the row with no change to its hooks.

## Consequences
- Until that P3.1 delta, AC-INV-044 holds for the Owner and Warehouse roles. For a Seller/Cashier in a tenant with
  two or more active warehouses, it holds by identifier only. In a single-warehouse tenant the column is hidden
  anyway (REQ-INV-012).
- This stage grants no permission and invents no field.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking (open item for the P3.1 delta).

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-037.md>>>
# ADR-INV-037 — Track placement and package of the INV test cases
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P4 (Test Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : test-gen · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : TC-INV-001, TC-INV-239, AC-INV-001, AC-INV-154, XM-INV-001, XM-INV-015, UXD-INV-001, UXD-INV-011, ADR-INV-024, ADR-INV-033

## Context
The engine derives one TC per AC and names one split unit per TC. Three choices are not mechanical for INV:
- Which track hosts an AC. Many ACs are observed at the API ("is returned", balances, moves, events). Others
  are observed on a screen ("is shown", menu, column, field). Some are both.
- Which unit a TC names when the AC has no REST operation. Provisioning, the daily near-expiry job, the
  architecture rule, events, entity invariants and the in-process `InventoryApi` (CON-INV-006 … 019, ADR-INV-024)
  have no `API-*`.
- Which frontend unit a TC names. Each screen is split into four units (F1 … F4), all of which trace the screen.

## Decision
1. **Track.** An AC whose Then is observable at the API or in-process surface gets a backend TC. An AC whose
   Then names a screen, menu, field, column or layout gets a frontend TC. An AC whose Then is a refusal "shown"
   on a screen, a permission AC, and an AC that reveals controls and keeps data unchanged gets one TC on each
   track. The guard holds: backend 172 TCs for 146 ACs + 15 XM, frontend 67 TCs for 45 ACs + 11 UXD.
2. **Backend package.** The SVC-API SUB holding the exercised `API-*` (CRUD, SEARCH). An in-process operation →
   `SVC-API-INT`; the TC cites the `InventoryApi` method and its contract item instead of an `API-*`.
   Provisioning, the daily job and the architecture rule → `CORE`. An entity invariant asserted without an
   endpoint response (move immutability, warehouse reference on every move, lot identity per Variant, the
   no-record default of Item stock settings) → the DATA-DOM SUB of that entity. Role-preset grants and the 403
   path → `SEC-BE`. An XM-derived TC → its `XM-INV-0nn` block.
3. **Frontend package.** Among the units of the screen whose `traces=` cite the AC or UXD: a server code routed
   to a field or message, or a query state → `F2-SCR-INV-0nn`; a client validator → `F3-SCR-INV-0nn`;
   visibility, route, layout or rendering → `F4-SCR-INV-0nn`; the menu and permission gate → `SEC-FE`. A UXD's
   "rendered" TC names the F3 unit when the foreign field is a search-form picker that F3 binds, otherwise F4;
   its "empty / failure" TC names the F2 unit that declares that state.
4. **Units with no TC.** No AC, XM or UXD derives a case for: backend `DOC`, `ALIGN-BE`; frontend `F1-SCR-INV-*`
   (types), `F3-SCR-INV-012`, `F4-SCR-INV-011`, `ALIGN-FE`. Both test plans list them in their COVERAGE section
   instead of inventing a case.

## Consequences
- Every AC has at least one TC across the two plans, and every XM and cited UXD has its TCs.
- If the profile does not flag the units of point 4 `no_tests`, C10.11 reports them. The fix is upstream (an AC,
  or a `no_tests` flag), not a fabricated case.
- No REQ, AC, RULE, API, SCR or code changes.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-038.md>>>
# ADR-INV-038 — Asserted texts and codes where the SRS, the catalogue and the API schema differ
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P4 (Test Plan)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : test-gen · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : AC-INV-078, AC-INV-098, AC-INV-106, AC-INV-111, AC-INV-113, AC-INV-144, AC-INV-147, RULE-INV-027, RULE-INV-033, RULE-INV-034, RULE-INV-044, RULE-INV-046, RULE-INV-047, API-INV-029, API-INV-036, API-INV-038, API-INV-045, API-INV-047

## Context
A test case copies messages from the SRS and asserts the catalogue code. Four places do not line up:
1. **AC text and RULE message differ.**
   - AC-INV-144 quotes «فعِّل مفتاح القدرة «التشغيلة والصلاحية» أولًا.» / "Switch on the lot and expiry
     capability flag first.". RULE-INV-044, the Error Catalog row INV-422-CAPABILITY-OFF and the frontend
     binding carry «فعِّل مفتاح القدرة الخاص بهذا الإعداد أولًا.» / "Switch on the capability flag for this
     setting first.".
   - AC-INV-147 quotes «… 3 أصناف تُتتبَّع بالتشغيلة. ألغِ تتبع التشغيلة لها أولًا.» / "… 3 Items are tracked
     by lot. Clear their lot tracking first.". RULE-INV-046 (the answer the plan states for CON-INV-019) gives
     «لا يمكن إيقاف «{flag}»: {count} أصناف تعتمد عليه. ألغِ الإعداد لها أولًا.» / "{flag} cannot be switched
     off: {count} Items depend on it. Clear the setting on them first.".
2. **Schema bound and RULE code on one field.** api-spec-inv.yaml bounds `OpeningStockRequest.rows` (maxItems
   1000) and `StockCountLineAddRequest.countedQty` (minimum 0). A schema validator could answer INV-400 before
   the service raises INV-422-LOAD-ROWS (RULE-INV-027) or INV-422-COUNTED-NEGATIVE (RULE-INV-047). The plan's
   Validations lines and the operations' `x-error-codes` name the RULE codes.
3. **A Given the API refuses to build.** AC-INV-111 starts from a DRAFT adjustment with a zero-change line. Both
   API-INV-036 and API-INV-037 refuse that line (RULE-INV-034) at save.
4. **A Given the screen cannot reach.** AC-INV-106 scans on a POSTED count. The frontend renders a POSTED count
   read-only, and hides its scan bar.

## Decision
1. TC-INV-045 and TC-INV-046 assert the code and the RULE message. That is the SRS A5 text the server returns
   and the frontend plan binds. Each TC states the AC wording as a recorded divergence. The SRS owner aligns the
   two ACs at the next INV delta.
2. The TCs assert the catalogue code (INV-422-…). If the delivered service answers INV-400 first, that is a
   finding against the plan, not a test change. Where the AC data allows, a TC satisfies the schema and still
   triggers the rule: TC-INV-033 sends `reasonCode` as an empty string for "no reason".
3. TC-INV-032 asserts the save-time refusal through API-INV-036. It then builds the AC's DRAFT below the API (a
   persisted fixture) and asserts the post-time refusal through API-INV-038.
4. The frontend TC of AC-INV-106 covers the reachable path. The count is open as DRAFT and is posted in another
   session. The scan then gets INV-409-DOCUMENT-CLOSED, routed by F2 (text RULE-INV-029, entry reloads read-only).

## Consequences
- No message is paraphrased. Every asserted text is an SRS text that a plan binds.
- Two SRS ACs carry wording the system will not produce. They are reported, not hidden.
- No REQ, RULE, API, SCR or code changes.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

<<<ADR: ADR-INV-039.md>>>
# ADR-INV-039 — Acceptance cases for F3-SCR-INV-012 and F4-SCR-INV-011
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : P4 (Test Plan) · repair round 1        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : test-gen · claude:opus
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : TC-INV-238, TC-INV-240, TC-INV-241, AC-INV-069, AC-INV-071, REQ-INV-063, REQ-INV-065, UXD-INV-011, SCR-INV-011, SCR-INV-012, ADR-INV-037

## Context
`gov.py analyze` (C10.11) refused the P4 plans: no test case named the frontend units `F3-SCR-INV-012` and
`F4-SCR-INV-011` on its `Package` line. ADR-INV-037 point 4 listed both as units nothing derives a case for. That
was wrong for both:
- `F3-SCR-INV-012` (valuation search schema) binds the UXD-INV-011 pickers (`variantPk` / `itemPk`). ADR-INV-037
  point 3 sends a UXD's "rendered" TC to the F3 unit when the foreign field is a search-form picker that F3 binds.
  TC-INV-238 is that case, but it named `F4-SCR-INV-012`.
- `F4-SCR-INV-011` (settings screen: the "Allow negative stock" switch and the horizon field) traces AC-INV-071,
  whose Given / When has the Owner save the negative-stock setting. P4 had placed AC-INV-071 on the backend track
  only (TC-INV-017).
- Once TC-INV-238 moves, `F4-SCR-INV-012` (valuation result table, grand total, detail drawer) would have no case.
  It traces AC-INV-069. REQ-INV-063 names the Owner as a reader of the valuation, so the figures AC-INV-069 states
  can be observed on SCR-INV-012.

## Decision
1. TC-INV-238 names `F3-SCR-INV-012`. This applies ADR-INV-037 point 3; the case itself is unchanged.
2. TC-INV-240 is derived from AC-INV-069 (REQ-INV-063), package `F4-SCR-INV-012`. The valuation screen renders the
   AC's figures: total quantity 20, average unit cost 23.0000, stock value 460.00, plus the grand total.
3. TC-INV-241 is derived from AC-INV-071 (REQ-INV-065), package `F4-SCR-INV-011`. The Owner switches "Allow negative
   stock" off and saves, and the screen keeps the value. The refusal of the later online issue stays on the backend
   track (TC-INV-017).
4. Both ACs are now on both tracks (ADR-INV-037 point 1). Each frontend case asserts only the UI half of its AC.
   The values come from the AC and no text is asserted beyond the SRS B3 label.
5. ADR-INV-037 point 4 no longer applies to `F3-SCR-INV-012` and `F4-SCR-INV-011`. It still applies to the other
   units it lists.

## Consequences
- The frontend plan holds TC-INV-173 … TC-INV-241 (69 cases, ratio 1.05 against 55 ACs + 11 UXD).
- No REQ, AC, RULE, API, SCR, UXD or code changes. No profile `no_tests` flag is needed for these two units.

## Status
ACCEPTED — non-breaking.

<<<END ADR>>>

# ADR-INV-040 — INV v1's XM edges to CAT are planned against delivered CAT v2 (resolution events acknowledged)
Status      : ACCEPTED
Stage       : gate analysis (feedback)        Module: INV        Version: v1
Lane        : operator · under Hesham's standing authorisation
Decided     : 2026-10-31
traces      : INV>CAT, XM-INV-001 … XM-INV-015, contract-cat (CAT v2) CON-CAT-001, CON-CAT-002, CON-CAT-005, CON-CAT-006

## Context
`gov.py graph` raised 16 resolution events into INV's manifest (`status.xm_events`), trigger `delivered`,
target CAT v2. These are the module edge INV>CAT and the 15 edges XM-INV-001 … XM-INV-015. An OPEN event
blocks INV's analysis gate until it is answered. The question each one asks: "your edge targets CAT, and
CAT is now delivered as v2. Does your plan hold against what was delivered?"

## Decision
Acknowledge all 16 events. No plan change is needed.
- The published CAT contract (`platform/contracts/contract-cat.md`) is CAT v2 (`Version : v2`, CON 18).
  It was published before INV's P1.5 to P4 ran, so every INV stage read the v2 contract.
- INV's backend execution plan (P3.1) cites only CAT v2 contract items: CON-CAT-001, CON-CAT-002,
  CON-CAT-005 and CON-CAT-006.
- INV's analysis is clean at the gate (`analyze gate:analysis` reports 0 critical · 0 major) against that
  contract.

## Consequences
- The 16 events are recorded as ANSWERED with this ADR (`gov.py answer-feedback`). They are not waived.
- If CAT publishes a v3 that changes a cited contract item, `gov.py graph` raises new events against v3,
  and those events are owed again.

<<<END ADR>>>

     "problem": "IDEMPOTENCY_KEY is indexed and not unique (D-P2-05). Reserve, receive and issue first look up 'moves/reservations with this key' (R-2/R-6) and only then lock balance rows.      "problem": "(a) The plan says reservations and issues of a Variant × warehouse 'serialise on the lot-less balance row'.      "problem": "Draft documents are saved and posted separately, but RULE-INV-007 (active warehouse), 018 (active Variant of a STANDARD Item), 037 (lot) and 040 (measure) trigger on submit or save, not on post.      "fix": "Add a step 0 to the posting engine: re-run RULE-INV-007/008/016/018/037/040 on every line before locking, and add 'on post' to those triggers.
